When a file bigger than 4MB is created
to preallocate
However for a filesystem with 1KB block size
block buddies used by the multiblock allocator is 2048
groups in the filesystem satisfies the search criteria in
ext4_mb_good_group(). Scanning all the filesystem groups impacts
performance.
This was demonstrated by using a freshly created
filesystem
column2: with caches dropped write before the test via

column1: /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches
column2: and with the filesystem mounted with

column1: nodelalloc and nodealloc
column2: nomballoc.  The time to write an 8 megabyte

column1: file using ""dd if=/dev/zero of=/mnt/test/fo bs=8k count=1k conv=fsync""
took 35.5091 seconds (236kB/s) with nodellaloc
(35.9 MB/s) with the nodelloc
it took several minutes to write 8MB!
This patch modifies the algorithm in ext4_mb_normalize_group_request to
calculate the number of blocks to allocate by taking into account the
maximum size of free blocks chunks handled by the multiblock allocator.
It has also been tested for filesystems with 2KB and 4KB block sizes to
ensure that those cases don't regress.
